integrity.count_basis: Fixed complete skew forms are therefore ordered matchings of coordinate labels, counted by the successive product of binomial choices.
integrity.euler_basis: Smooth projectivity and Bialynicki--Birula decomposition identify Euler characteristic with the number of isolated fixed points.
integrity.first_public_date_basis: The arXiv record for math/9808114 lists version 1 on 1998-08-27.
integrity.fixed_point_basis: A diagonal one-parameter subgroup with binary-separated basis weights forces every fixed projective two-form on every coordinate kernel to be a single coordinate wedge.
integrity.object_basis: Thaddeus defines complete skew forms as successive nonzero two-forms on iterated kernels and identifies their moduli space with an iterated blow-up along the Pluecker Grassmannian and its secant varieties.
integrity.primary_slot_basis: The archival source lists Mathematics Subject Classification 14M15 as Primary.

scientific_limitations: The theorem determines ordinary Euler characteristic, not the full Poincare polynomial or cohomology ring.
It concerns the standard complete-skew-form compactification and not arbitrary compactifications of the maximal-rank locus.
An older cell-decomposition or wonderful-compactification computation could imply the same formula even though targeted searches did not locate one.
title: Euler characteristic of complete skew forms
